subject: RFI: Reservation — ingestion concurrency & GPU-family tradeoffs
messages:
From: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@parkplace.ai>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@parkplace.ai, ops-eng@parkplace.ai
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: Peak ingest profile & reservation ask

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this RFI. Quick context: ParkPlace is evaluating a dedicated reservation for our real-time summarization/ingest flow. We expect sustained traffic of ~2M inference requests/day with spikes up to 4.5M on business days. Average request size is ~60 tokens (user prompt + system prompt), with an average generated output of ~120 tokens. Our p95 latency target is 350ms and p99 target is 700ms.

Can you provide:
- Expected tokens/sec and concurrent streams per GPU family (H100 / A100 / A10G / L4) for our profile (avg seq ~200 tokens total).
- Suggested reservation mix (committed GPUs by family) to meet 2M sustained and absorb 4.5M spikes with burst lanes.
- How batching/caching and prefix KV cache change the recommendation (we have repeat prompts for ~22% of requests).
- Any recommended SLA exceptions or fallback playbooks (we need a draft for procurement).

Attached: parkplace-rfi-dataset-profile.csv with hourly distribution and tail percentiles. Procurement will need a formal workbook.

Thanks — would like a first-pass reply by EOD Wednesday PT.

Best,
Sandeep Rao
Head of Platform Engineering
ParkPlace AI

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@parkplace.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Peak ingest profile & reservation ask

Hi Sandeep — thanks for the profile and the CSV; useful signal here. Below is a concise first-pass recommendation and the assumptions baked into our workbook (attached). I'll schedule a follow-up workshop to validate with a live replay.

Top-level recommendation (first pass):
- Baseline committed pool: mix of 10 x H100 + 25 x A100 to meet sustained 2M/day with headroom. H100s sized for tail-heavy, low-latency slices; A100s handle steady throughput and lower-cost burst.
- Burst lanes: additional autoscale capacity (uncommitted) to absorb up to 4.5M spikes. For contract planning, propose a 25% burst credit pool tied to your monthly commit.
- Caching: with ~22% identical repeat prompts, prefix KV caching yields ~18–25% token savings in practice; we modeled both 0% and 22% cache scenarios in the workbook.
- Batching settings: conservative continuous-batching with max batch 48 for H100 and 32 for A100 to preserve tail.

Measured model throughput (profile assumptions: seq_len = 200 tokens total, FP16 / quantized runtime where supported):
- H100 (FP16, batch=32): ~5,800 tokens/sec; practical concurrent streams target: 20-28 streams for p95 latency <350ms.
- A100 (FP16, batch=32): ~4,100 tokens/sec; concurrent streams target: 12-18.
- A10G (INT8 quantized, batch=24): ~2,100 tokens/sec; good mid-tier capacity for cost-sensitive steady workloads.
- L4 (INT8, batch=16): ~1,400 tokens/sec; useful for small assistant endpoints, not recommended as main reservation for this workload.

How we mapped to your numbers: sustained 2M req/day @ average 180 tokens/request ~= 360M tokens/day ~= 4,167 tokens/sec sustained. Accounting for inefficiencies, gives the 10 H100 + 25 A100 baseline above. With 22% caching your sustained requirement drops ~18% in tokens/sec and reduces A100 count by ~6–8.

Operational notes:
- We recommend enabling KV-prefix caching for the high-repeat subset and a conservative continuous-batch policy.
- Canary model variants: use a lighter quantized variant for tail traffic automatically when primary pool is congested. That requires an explicit fallback policy in the contract (we include language in the attached sla-exception-request.pdf).

I've attached redwood-reservation-recommendation-v2.xlsx with full math, sensitivity scenarios (cache/no-cache, 3x / 2x spike models), and a suggested SLA exception draft for procurement.

Next steps:
1) Review workbook (I put a README tab explaining inputs).
2) Schedule a 90-min capacity validation replay with your ops team + our infra engineers (I propose Thu 13 May or Mon 17 May).
3) Procurement: we can provide a one-page commitment summary + exception wording for DocuSign.

On availability: happy to take the workshop on Thu 13 May 10–11:30 PT.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Sandeep Rao <sandeep@parkplace.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Peak ingest profile & reservation ask

Adding a complementary viewpoint on GPU mix and contingency:

I agree with Naomi's baseline but suggest an alternative that reduces committed TCO while keeping latency targets:
- Commit: 8 x H100 + 18 x A100 + 10 x A10G (A10G used for steady-state lower-priority traffic).
- Rationale: A10G provides a cheaper committed baseline for predictable low-priority slices (billing/log summaries) while H100s cover p99 tail-sensitive requests.

Additional throughput benchmarks (same seq ~200 tokens, optimized kernels):
- H100 w/ batching tuned: 6,200 tokens/sec (batch 48, aggressive kernel selection) — but note tail risk if batch shapes vary.
- A100 tuned: 4,300 tokens/sec (batch 40).
- A10G quantized: 2,250 tokens/sec.

Concurrency guidance: keep per-GPU concurrency target conservative when you care about p99. For H100 aim for 20 streams; for A100 14; for A10G 8. We included a booking worksheet that computes expected p95/p99 given concurrency and batch-policy; see redwood-reservation-recommendation-v2.xlsx -> Sensitivity tab.

If ParkPlace wants a lower committed spend, we can trade 7 A100s to 10 A10G and expand burst credits. I'll be on the call for the replay to run live replays.

— Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@parkplace.ai>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@parkplace.ai, ops-eng@parkplace.ai
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Peak ingest profile & reservation ask

Thanks Naomi and Karthik — helpful detail. A couple quick procurement/ops follow-ups:

1) Procurement needs a DocuSign-ready one-page commitment summary + the SLA exception text you mentioned. Can you provide that by next Tue EOD?
2) Ops: can Redwood commit to a validation replay and provide the per-GPU concurrency tool/command we can use to reproduce your workbook numbers? Our platform team will want the exact script.
3) Can you confirm what telemetry you need from our side for the replay (hourly historic, tail logs, sample requests)?

Also attaching a short procurement checklist on our side — the team will review the redwood-reservation-recommendation-v2.xlsx and circle back with questions.

If we can lock the one-pager and replay date next week procurement can fast-track.

Thanks,
Sandeep

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@parkplace.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 16:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Peak ingest profile & reservation ask

Sandeep — attaching the one-pager and the replay checklist (see attachments). Quick answers inline: 

1) DocuSign one-pager: attached as redwood-reservation-recommendation-v2.xlsx (Summary tab has the commitment language). We'll also send a DocuSign packet after you confirm final GPU counts.
2) Repro scripts: we'll share a small toolkit (bash + python) that runs our load-replay harness, plus a lightweight `gpu-concurrency-bench` binary we use internally. For the replay you only need to provide: historical hourly CSV (you already sent), a 30–60 minute request sample set (anonymized), and your target model variant name.
3) Telemetry: hourly request counts, sample requests, tail latency traces (p95/p99), and a 1-hour continuous tail dump for the busiest hour.

Proposed replay windows: Mon 17 May 10:00–11:30 PT (preferred) or Tue 18 May 08:00–09:30 PT. Please confirm.

I'll loop in the contracts lead for the DocuSign flow once you confirm the final numbers. Happy to run through the workbook live on the replay call.

Best regards,
Naomi Feldman
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
